audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Skill/Gnar/Gnar. Packet says Gnar,Gnar,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Zac and the whys[] prose matches the packet on all four disputed stages.
audit.why: whys[0] says Mini wins the first trade 'clean' — a Gnar stage, marked Skill. whys[2] ends 'the edge flattens to even' — marked Gnar. whys[5] ends 'neither side clearly owns the window' — marked Gnar. whys[6] opens 'Zac out-scales' and late says he reclaims the lane at two items — marked Gnar.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Zac as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer spikes said 'Stridebreaker'; Zac's real spikes are Elastic Slingshot's cooldown decay and Let's Bounce! at 6.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21s at rank 1 but 9s at rank 5 — that more-than-halving is why 'bait his engage and commit' works early and stops working later, and the page states neither number. Let's Bounce! is 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Phase whys and the cooldown block now carry the 21s-to-9s decay and the 120s ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never states that Stretching Strikes is an auto-attack reset, never states that Unstable Matter and Cell Division deal PERCENT MAX HEALTH, and dontsFull[0] ('Let him eat blobs') carries filler text that never mentions healing at all — while dosFull[1] is titled 'Build MR' with a body about boomerangs.
audit.why: All three flagged missing interactions land here. Percent-max-health damage from both his passive and W is why the recommended Plated Steelcaps reads the trade wrong — armour does nothing against it, and stacking HP actively makes it worse. Cell Division blobs refund the chip you spent the whole lane accumulating, so Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade. And the Q reset means his burst opens on a wind-up, not a visible ability cast.
audit.corrected: Stated the auto reset and its tell, the percent-max-health damage on both passive and W (with W's 5s cooldown and 350 range), and the anti-heal requirement against Cell Division.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: content writes 'Let's Bounce' without the exclamation mark in whys[4], spikes[2].text and mid.
audit.why: The ability is Let's Bounce! — the exclamation mark is part of the name, which is why the name-checker flagged all three.
audit.corrected: Punctuation restored in all three strings.

edits.before: This is where it goes even — Gnar's whole mid game is Rage RNG. With Mega up, a Wallop line-stun into a wall-flung GNAR! is a clean kill, and you should force it the instant his Slingshot is on cooldown. Without the transform you are a ranged poke champ chipping a tank who walks over his passive blobs and heals the chip right back, so the damage just resets. Never blow Mega on a poke trade — bait his Slingshot engage, let it whiff, then commit the full combo while his only gap-closer is down. From level 6 his Let's Bounce ult also threatens to bounce in and answer a sloppy Mega commit, so pick the moment carefully.

notes: MIRROR: zac__gnar was already audited, and its notes say the full layer there wrongly named GNAR! as the cooldown to track and that the stun was reattributed to Wallop (W). My edits here are consistent with that — I attribute the stun to Wallop and the wall-stun to GNAR!, and I do not claim Gnar's threat is gated by his ultimate's cooldown. My chart (Gnar,Gnar,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Zac) should invert cleanly to Zac's side; the mirror findings did not include its chart values so I could not verify row by row. Packet suspectNames were both near-misses on punctuation/wording rather than fabricated names — 'Let's Bounce' was missing its exclamation mark and is fixed in three strings; 'Zac's Elastic Slingshot' in wants.you[2] is correct as written and left alone. DERIVED FLAG IGNORED: the kit file puts a 'grounding' flag on Elastic Slingshot, which would mean it shuts off Gnar's Hop — a decisive interaction if true. Riot's own description is just 'attaches his arms to the ground and stretches back, launching himself forward', with no grounding effect. Per the rule that the description beats a misfiring flag I wrote nothing about it, but it is worth a ruling because it would change every disengage line on this page.
unverified: Whether Elastic Slingshot actually grounds — the kit's derived flag says yes, Riot's description says nothing. Not asserted either way in any edit.
